title: Thermodynamic Irreversibility from Inaccessible Endogenous Quantum Histories
abstract: Microscopic unitary dynamics preserves all fine information, yet an isolated finite system can show a robust thermodynamic window in which the entropy associated with a restricted record rises. We ask why information hidden from the current record usually fails to rebuild a low-entropy macrostate. For a fixed projective record, every finite step separates exactly into the evolution predicted from the record alone and an exact correction carried by unresolved microscopic structure. The record-only contribution starts only at second order in time, so all instantaneous change of the record comes from hidden currents between macrostates. We derive the exact entropy rate, separate entropy-spreading from return-oriented currents, and resolve those currents into energy-gap amplitudes. Transitions with the same gap add coherently, revealing how the Hamiltonian and the microscopic state organize hidden information for return. In interacting mixing dynamics the current power is spread over many frequencies; free and deliberately commensurate controls progressively concentrate it, and the engineered dynamics reconstructs a low-entropy macrostate. An independent distribution-level test separates hidden dynamical activity from finite-step return, and an exact classical measure-preserving counterpart shows which parts of the construction are not uniquely quantum. Within the specified record and observation window, irreversibility is therefore not loss of microscopic information, but the failure of that information to organize currents that restore macroscopic order.
summary: This theoretical work tackles the paradox of irreversibility in unitary quantum systems by showing that the apparent loss of entropy is due to the failure of hidden microscopic information to organize into restorative macroscopic currents. The authors develop exact mathematical tools to separate entropy generation from these return currents, providing a deep, quantum-mechanical understanding of the Second Law.
main_problem: The paper addresses the origin of thermodynamic irreversibility in an isolated quantum system whose underlying dynamics are unitary and information-preserving.
main_result: Irreversibility is shown not to be the loss of microscopic information, but rather the failure of that hidden information to organize the quantum currents necessary to restore macroscopic order.
method: The authors derive an exact entropy rate by splitting the state into a macroscopic 'record' part and an unresolved 'hidden' part, analyzing the resulting currents via spectral decomposition.
model_or_system: The analysis considers an isolated quantum system evolving unitarily, focusing on the dynamics observed through a fixed projective record. The theory is tested using models like hard-core and Bose-Hubbard chains.
key_observables: Thermodynamic Entropy Rate ($\dot{S}_R$), Observational Deficit ($I_R$), and 'hidden currents' ($J_{RR'}$).
important_parameters: The analysis is restricted to finite observation windows and specific projective records; the thermodynamic limit is not fully established.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the specified records and observation windows; heat and work require additional boundary specifications.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first defining the information deficit, then deriving the exact entropy rate by separating spreading from return currents, and finally comparing the finite-step evolution to the orbit-average evolution to establish the physical meaning of irreversibility.
why_interesting: It provides a rigorous, quantum mechanical framework for understanding the Second Law of Thermodynamics in isolated systems by quantifying the role of coherence and hidden degrees of freedom in macroscopic irreversibility.
